chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman and Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Al-Sawiq digests the heads (crusts of the stomach).

key_terms.الرُّءُوسَ: The heads; here referring to the upper part or crust of the stomach where food first settles.
key_terms.السَّوِيقُ: A traditional food made from roasted flour, often mixed with water or milk.
key_terms.يَهْضِمُ: Digests; breaks down food in the stomach.

ai.seo_question: What are the digestive benefits of Sawiq according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the digestive efficacy of *Sawiq*, a traditional flour-based food, noting its ability to aid digestion in the 'heads' (upper stomach). This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of integrating practical dietary medicine with spiritual and physical well-being, emphasizing simple, wholesome foods as prophetic remedies. The term 'heads' (*al-ru'us*) is interpreted by commentators as referring to the upper regions of the stomach or the head of the food's digestion process, underscoring the precision of traditional medical knowledge in Imami teachings.

en.hubeali:
